title: B2 · L12 — Participle clauses
description: Cláusulas de participio con -ing y -ed para simplificar oraciones. Recurso esencial de la escritura académica y periodística B2.

questions.prompt: Situación: reescribes una frase para un artículo de estilo periodístico.
questions.question: Simplify: 'Because she was tired, she went to bed early.'
options: Being tired, she went to bed early.
To be tired, she went to bed early.
Tired she being, she went to bed early.
Was tired, she went to bed early.
questions.explanation: La cláusula de participio con -ing sustituye 'because/as/since + sujeto + be'. 'Being tired' equivale a 'As she was tired'. La estructura elimina el conector y el verbo auxiliar, dejando una construcción más compacta y elegante — muy típica del inglés escrito formal y periodístico.
examples: Feeling exhausted after the trip, he took a two-hour nap. → narrativa fluida
Being hungry and too tired to cook, she ordered a pizza.

questions.prompt: Redactas la introducción a un ensayo sobre literatura.
questions.question: Which sentence uses a past participle clause correctly?
options: Written in 1850, the novel remains popular today.
Writing in 1850, the novel remains popular.
The novel that written in 1850 is popular.
Being written in 1850, the novel is popular.
questions.explanation: La cláusula de participio pasado tiene siempre sentido PASIVO. 'Written in 1850' = 'which was written in 1850'. Error típico: usar '-ing' pensando que es más 'activo', pero eso cambiaría el sujeto (la novela no estaba escribiendo, alguien la escribió). Regla mnemotécnica: -ing = activo; -ed/PP = pasivo.
examples: Built in the 12th century, the castle now attracts thousands of tourists a year.
Made from 100% recycled materials, this bag is genuinely eco-friendly. → registro ecomarketing

questions.statement: Las cláusulas de participio siempre se refieren al mismo sujeto que la cláusula principal.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Si el sujeto del participio no coincide con el de la cláusula principal, se produce un 'dangling participle' — considerado error grave en escritura formal y examen. Es uno de los fallos más frecuentes al escribir en inglés, incluso entre nativos poco cuidadosos.
examples: Correct: Walking home, I saw an old friend. → 'I' walked y 'I' vi
Incorrect (dangling): Walking home, the rain started pouring. → la lluvia no camina, error

questions.text: Having finished her assignment, she treated herself to a well-deserved cup of tea.
questions.explanation: 'Having + PP' indica una acción COMPLETADA antes de la principal, equivale a 'After she had finished'. Connected speech: 'having finished' se enlaza 'hævɪŋ-fɪnɪʃt', y 'treated herself' fluye con la /d/ suave. 'Well-deserved' es colocación fija con guión — enfatiza que el descanso es merecido tras esfuerzo.
examples: Having read the whole report twice, he finally understood the client's concerns.
Having lived abroad for a decade, she spoke five languages fluently. → biografía profesional

questions.prompt: Simplificas una descripción en una novela.
questions.question: Rewrite: 'The man who is standing over there is my uncle.'
options: The man stood over there is my uncle.
The man standing over there is my uncle.
The man to stand over there is my uncle.
The man stand over there is my uncle.
questions.explanation: El participio -ing sustituye 'who/which + BE + -ing'. 'The man standing' = 'the man who is standing'. Es una reducción muy común en descripciones habladas y escritas — hace el estilo más ligero. Cuidado: 'stood' aquí sería pasivo/pasado (fue puesto de pie), lo cual no encaja.
examples: The woman wearing the red dress is my sister — the one by the bar. → descripción social
The children playing in the garden are all my nephews and nieces.

questions.statement: 'Damaged in the storm, the roof needed repairing' tiene una cláusula de participio pasado con sentido pasivo.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Damaged' equivale a 'which was damaged'. Los participios pasados en cláusulas reducidas SIEMPRE tienen sentido pasivo — algo le fue hecho al sujeto. Este patrón es muy común en informes técnicos, crónicas periodísticas y descripciones históricas.
examples: Written entirely by hand, the letter felt intimate and personal. → detalle emocional
Destroyed during the 1944 bombing, the cathedral was later rebuilt stone by stone.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada cláusula participial con su continuación lógica:

pairs.right: she took a deep breath before speaking.
I noticed the flowers had bloomed.
the house still looks brand new.

questions.explanation: Combina los tres tipos principales: -ing (acción activa/simultánea), participio pasado (pasivo/estado), y 'having + PP' (acción previa completada). En todos los casos, el sujeto del participio DEBE coincidir con el sujeto de la cláusula principal — es la regla de oro.
examples: Sitting by the window, she watched the rain streaking down the glass. → escena narrativa
Built in 1900 and lovingly restored, the theatre remains a city landmark.

questions.prompt: Identifica el error gramatical clásico en escritura descuidada.
questions.question: Which sentence contains a dangling participle (error)?
options: Running down the street, I tripped on a rock.
Running down the street, the rock made me trip.
While running down the street, I tripped on a rock.
I tripped on a rock while running down the street.
questions.explanation: En la opción B, 'running' se refiere gramaticalmente al sujeto 'the rock' — pero las piedras no corren. Es el ejemplo de manual del 'dangling participle'. Se corrige asegurando que el sujeto del participio sea el mismo que el de la cláusula principal, o reescribiendo con 'while + sujeto + verbo'.
examples: Incorrect: Reading the newspaper, the coffee spilled all over the table.
Correct: Reading the newspaper, I accidentally knocked over my coffee.

questions.target: Having worked in three different countries, she has developed a truly global perspective.
questions.explanation: 'Having worked' + resultado presente — fórmula típica de introducción biográfica en entrevistas, LinkedIn, discursos de bienvenida. Prosodia: pausa suave tras 'countries' para marcar la transición entre cláusulas. Nativos añaden intensificadores como 'truly', 'genuinely' o 'quite' para reforzar sin sonar exagerados.
examples: Having lived in Southeast Asia for five years, he understands the business culture there deeply.
Having studied both economics and psychology, she can bridge the two fields effortlessly.

questions.prompt: Reescribes una frase para una narración fluida.
questions.question: Rewrite: 'After I had eaten dinner, I watched a film.'
options: Eating dinner, I watched a film.
Eaten dinner, I watched a film.
Having eaten dinner, I watched a film.
To eat dinner, I watched a film.
questions.explanation: 'Having + PP' (participio perfecto) indica una acción completada ANTES de la principal — es la reducción exacta de 'After I had eaten'. La opción A ('Eating') implicaría simultaneidad (verlo mientras comía), no secuencia. La distinción es clave para mantener el orden temporal correcto.
examples: Having finished work early, he decided to head to the beach for sunset.
Having read the whole book, she wrote a thoughtful review on her blog.

questions.statement: Las cláusulas de participio son comunes en escritura formal porque hacen las oraciones más concisas.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Reducen la extensión, evitan repeticiones de sujeto y verbo auxiliar, y elevan el registro estilístico. Son herramienta fundamental en escritura académica, periodística y literaria. Sin embargo, en hablado casual suenan libresco — mejor evitarlas en conversación relajada.
examples: Long: The report, which was written by the committee, is very detailed.
Short: Written by the committee, the report is very detailed. → registro formal

questions.text: Surrounded by mountains and lakes, the village offers breathtaking views all year round.
questions.explanation: Participio pasado con sentido pasivo, típico de descripciones turísticas y textos de viajes (Lonely Planet, blogs de viajes). Prosodia elegante, pausa suave tras 'lakes'. Connected speech: 'surrounded by' se enlaza fluido, y 'breathtaking' recibe énfasis emocional. 'All year round' es colocación fija — nunca 'all the year'.
examples: Located just five minutes from the beach, the hotel is a favourite among honeymooners.
Built on a dramatic hilltop, the medieval castle dominates the whole valley below.

questions.prompt: Describes una obra de arte en una guía de museo.
questions.question: Complete: '___ from a distance, the sculpture looks like a bird.'
options: To see
Seeing
Seen
Been seen
questions.explanation: 'Seen from a distance' equivale a 'when seen from a distance' — participio pasado con sentido pasivo (la escultura ES vista). 'Seeing' sería activo y cambiaría el sujeto. Es el patrón típico para describir cómo se percibe algo desde una perspectiva concreta.
examples: Viewed from above, the field forms a perfect geometric circle. → foto aérea
Read aloud, the poem sounds even more haunting than on the page.

questions.target: Not knowing what to say, I remained silent for what felt like an eternity.
questions.explanation: Cláusula de participio negativa: 'NOT' va antes del participio, nunca después. Prosodia: pausa reflexiva tras 'say', y énfasis emotivo en 'eternity'. Es una estructura muy natural para narrar momentos incómodos o de bloqueo emocional. Nativos añaden 'honestly', 'genuinely' para intensificar.
examples: Not wanting to interrupt their conversation, I just quietly waited by the door.
Not having eaten anything all day, I was absolutely starving by 7 p.m. → excusa cotidiana

questions.prompt: Identifica qué frase expresa causa mediante participio.
questions.question: Which sentence uses a participle clause to express reason?
options: Being ill, she stayed at home.
She was ill and stayed at home.
She stayed at home because she was ill.
The illness kept her home.
questions.explanation: 'Being ill' equivale a 'Because/As she was ill' — la cláusula participial puede expresar CAUSA, TIEMPO, CONDICIÓN o simplemente descripción según el contexto. Es una construcción polivalente y elegante. Las otras opciones expresan la misma idea pero con estructura convencional.
examples: Feeling unwell after lunch, he cancelled his afternoon meetings. → causa
Living so far from town, they rarely visited their old friends. → causa/circunstancia
